newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Landcorp reports NZ$19.9 mln year net profit.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Landcorp reports NZ$19.9 mln year net profit.

text.p: New Zealand's state-owned Land Corporation Ltd announced a NZ$19.9 million net profit after tax for the year ended June 30, 1996, in its annual report released on Monday.
This compared with an annual net profit of $24.05 million in 1995.
Gross operating revenue was $66.5 million with total expenditure of $69.3 million resulting in a net operating loss of $2.8 million.

However, profits of $22.5 million from the sale of financial and land assets resulted in an overall net profit before tax of NZ$19.7 million. Group net profit after tax and minority interests was $19.9 million.
"The year under review has been a difficult one for Landcorp's core farming business," Landcorp said,
"Market conditions affecting sheep and beef farmers generally and the effect of the Crown settlement of Maori land grievances on Landcorp's asset rationalisation, have limited overall profitability."
Interim dividends totalling $25.6 million were paid during the year and included $12.6 million from the redemption of all remaining preference shares in Landcorp Investments Ltd.
Landcorp said provision had been made for payment of a final dividend of $11.4 million on October 31, 1996.

The total dividend of $37 million represented 29.6 cents per ordinary share. "This dividend is sourced from a combination of profits earned and net capital released from the sale of non-core assets," Landcorp said.

It said $47.2 million was received from the disinvestment of assets surplus to the core business; $18 million was applied to reinvestment; $49.8 million was paid in dividends, and net borrowing totalled $25.1 million.
Landcorp said its results were severely affected by very low cattle prices. Wool prices were also adversely affected by world demand.

"The low profitability of beef and wool is expected to persist into 1997. Industry sheep and beef cattle numbers are likely to fall and land use will continue to change towards alternatives such as dairying and forestry," Landcorp said.
"Landcorp has moved to reduce its dependency on beef in particular with further investment in deer and in dairying."

Landcorp said difficulties with Maori land claim issues had delayed the farm sales process, and cooperation with the Crown to assist in the settlement of Treaty claims would mean the loss of some core large scale farm properties which would be difficult to replace.
"Profits and cash flows from Landcorp Investments Ltd will substantially decrease from now on, with the reduced number and value of assets remaining in this company," Landcorp said.
